# Cennini: the same written form as operation and made object

Status: **RAW_UNREVIEWED, external source only; not a selected experiment or a manuscript reading.** Bounded task started 2026-09-20 06:49:15 UTC, deadline 07:09:15 UTC.

## Complete owned unit

Cennino Cennini, *Trattato della pittura*, ed. Giuseppe Tambroni, Rome1821, complete chapters CLXIII–CLXVI, printed pp147–151, PDF pages203–207. The [public primary PDF](https://archive.org/download/dicenninocennini00cenn/dicenninocennini00cenn.pdf) has SHA256 `5404f9767fcc5651484c5752f2b819bfa2663f7f5ea0176e0c32a6991a0f95c3`. All five pages were viewed natively. The companion `CENNINI_PROCESS_PRODUCT_SOURCE_20260920.json` contains the complete normalized Italian main text and headings, a 29-position content inventory, grammatical occurrences, distinct entities, references, alternatives and editorial difficulties. Neither those inventory positions nor source words are proposed target units.

This is one connected four-chapter workshop section. CLXIII announces the art and its utility; CLXIV prepares the model and casting enclosure; CLXV supplies breathing apparatus; CLXVI makes/removes a first form, casts a second object inside it, removes the outer shell and ends with a metal-casting possibility and requirement for skilled masters. The preliminary work, qualifications, analogy, rationale, optional branch, delayed temporal instruction and closing craft qualification remain in scope. The metal possibility itself is not a fully specified foundry recipe.

The work predates1450: its oldest surviving copy, Florence BML Plut.78.23, bears a1437 copying date. The [1859 editors' preface](https://it.wikisource.org/wiki/Il_libro_dell%27arte/Prefazione) distinguishes that colophon from a date of authorial composition. The [critical editor's research account](https://www.memofonte.it/home/files/pdf/XV_2015_RICOTTA.pdf), printedp27 n1, identifies the1437 witness and later copies. Our exact wording belongs to1821, which follows a later copy; this is not a diplomatic edition of the medieval folios. The corresponding1859 chapters are CLXXXI–CLXXXIV, not identically numbered chapters. Institutional witness: [Plut.78.23](https://tecabml.contentdm.oclc.org/digital/collection/plutei/id/1094410). Exact medieval spelling still needs independent collation.

## Actual form and grammatical distinction

The literal form **impronta** appears in two finite verbal constructions and four nominal constructions in this owned section:

| Locus | Written construction | Required role |
|---|---|---|
| CLXIV heading | `In che modo s’impronta di naturale la faccia` | Process: how one molds/the face is molded; `si` and the finite predicate provide grammatical scope. |
| CLXIV ending | `siccome vuoi che la impronta della pasta vegna` | Prospective formed object, with article, material specification and its own predicate. |
| CLXV heading | `alla persona, della quale s’impronta la faccia` | Process on the live person's face; breathing apparatus belongs to that person. |
| CLXVI heading | `Come si getta di gesso sul vivo la impronta` | Object of casting, qualified by gypsum and live model. |
| CLXVI final result | `la effigia, o ver la filosomia, o vero impronta` | Produced likeness, coordinated with other object nouns after `arai`. |
| CLXVI metal possibility | `fare buttare la detta impronta di rame` | Previously described representation to be cast in a further material. |

This is original Italian grammar, not switching modern translations to save a reading. It is also not a claim that `s’impronta` and `la impronta` are identical complete written phrases: the same lexical form occurs within different explicit constructions. The infinitive `improntare` and inflected `impronti` additionally identify the process family, but are not counted as the exact form `impronta`.

The weaker candidate `Tempera con la medesima tempera` in XIX was rejected for this task: the nominal *tempera* there denotes a binder/preparation or consistency used as input, and does not securely name the direct output of that precise tempering action. It is not a second proposal.

## Coupled consequence and object identity

The live model's face is oiled; plaster compound sets around it and is removed as a mask/form. A subsequent gypsum preparation is poured into that first form. Optional brick powder is added only to this later preparation. After half a day, or at most a day, the outer shell is broken: the text expressly identifies it as **the first form** and requires the represented nose and remainder to survive. An earlier optional sawing operation weakens the outside but must not pass through; although narrated later, its written `innanzi che l’empia` places it before filling.

Thus there are at least a living model, a first plaster form and a second plaster cast. First and second are physically distinct even though *forma*, *confezione* and *impronta* participate in an overlapping reference chain. Preparation by the same method is not reuse of the same hardened mass. The second form reproduces the face through two successive transfers; a one-stage description ends at the first mold and does not account for the second fill/destructive release.

The geometric interpretation is negative relief for the first cavity and positive relief for the second likeness. That polarity is an inference from the cast-inside-cast construction, **not source terminology or a directly owned diagram**. The historical text owns the first/second distinction, the first object's destruction and the second likeness's preservation. No sign arithmetic, globally mirrored coordinates or manuscript picture ownership is assumed.

Distinct rivals under the same source grammar fail differently. Treating every occurrence as a verb loses article-led objects and the effigy coordination. Treating every occurrence as a noun loses the finite *si*-predications and their face arguments. Treating all repeated object descriptions as the same physical item cannot preserve the second nose while destroying the first outer form. Treating sentence order as execution order violates the optional saw instruction's explicit before-filling condition. These are source-semantic consequences, not tested manuscript discriminators.

## Textual limits and writing debt

Tambroni explicitly marks the removal/posture wording onp150 as difficult. His proposed correction to `o impretendosi` is retained separately in the JSON, not silently substituted. The later metal clause says `poichè hai la prima` after the destructive-release account; whether it resumes an earlier opportunity, a first form in a generic method or another model relation is not resolved. We do not make a broken first mold magically reusable. The list of metals expresses possibilities rather than a series of completed casts.

No complete compact writer is supplied. Ordinary Italian supplies clitics, determiners, clause syntax, temporal phrases and discourse references. A future reading hypothesis would have to bind their functional counterparts through one shared grammar; it could not freely choose noun/verb or identity independently for each target occurrence. Exact Italian spelling, suffixes and word counts supply no target alphabet or grouping rule. There is no target passage nomination, new lexical value, decoder, model execution or scientific reopening.

## Predecessors and retained stops

Bounded navigation used live route, composition topic, ideas searches for Cennini/tempera/impronta/nominalization/process-product/casting and route-check. Empty lexical hits were not treated as proof of novelty.

- IDEA000390's complete Theophilus named-mixture source card was read. It owns named recipe inheritance and case/layer roles, not an identical lexical form functioning as verb and result noun. GDT989's fixed three-stage/header rejection remains; this source is not a header-code revision.
- IDEA000061 and its primary decision `research_registry/decisions/lp_root_four_relation_design_reviews.json` retain the missing independent output/input-state observation. Reusing one inherited gloss makes transfer equality automatic. Cennini's independently written first-form destruction/second-object preservation is external evidence, not that missing manuscript observation.
- GDT719's METHOD was read: shared result readings do not establish shared `dy` morphology. Root's separate primary review additionally retains GDT720 and IL021's cross-construction root/state-capacity stop. No result-gloss-to-root export is made here.
- GDT832's complete REPORT was read: context recovered wholeword values in a known mixed Latin control, but the family factor supplied no extra recovery and full reconstruction failed. Known roles/boundaries were supplied; this source does not solve unknown segmentation or rescue that control.

Scope receipt: no raw Voynich, reserve, manuscript image or GDT992 artifact was opened. The full IDEA61 primary-decision JSON unexpectedly included old GDT701/702 EVA/locus/renderer quotations; the GDT719 method also names its old form-class examples. The accidental review exposure was disclosed to root immediately and was not used to choose or fit a target. No blindness claim is made. All existing cards/source bytes remain unchanged; no global refresh, commit, process termination or external contact occurred.
